newsitem.title: USA: American States exploring sale of company.
newsitem.headline: American States exploring sale of company.

text.p: American States Financial Corp said it has hired Goldman Sachs to help it explore its strategic options, including the possible sale of the company.

Lincoln National Corp confirmed it was considering the sale of its 83 percent-owned property-casualty business, which has a market value of about $2 billion based on the share price and number of shares outstanding.
"Consolidation trends in the property-casualty industry may make this an opportune time to fully realize the value of the company," said American States Chief Executive Robert A. Anker.
"We do not intend to make any further statement until the process is complete."

Sources familiar with the situation said Goldman has been sounding out potential acquirers, but said they believed the process was in its early stages and that the financial books have yet to go out to prospective buyers.

Potential acquirers could include Travelers Property Casualty Corp, CNA Financial Corp and Liberty Mutual Insurance Co, as well as some foreign insurers such as Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV, Aegon NV and Fortis AG.
Earlier this month, SAFECO Corp also was rumored to be a possible buyer.
Travelers and CNA declined comment. Liberty Mutual was not immediately available for comment. SAFECO previously declined comment.
